content.comment_body: Hello all, I am a researcher at a university and we need to use PLCs for a project. Our goal is to build a system capable of taking a 25KW 3-phase AC input and activating just one of several outputs at a time. For example, we have 3 pumps and only one should be active at once, with energy consumption measured for each. We want to remotely control the system using Python and measure each pump’s consumption. The system should be suitable for industrial environments. Would [product_name] work for this purpose? Thank you.

Hello [user_name], welcome. If you use the current [product_name] model, you don't need Python for remote control. The latest version includes two web servers: a simple one that mirrors the device interface and an advanced one that displays custom user-made sites in a browser. To measure the pump energy consumption, you’d need extra hardware like current and voltage transformers providing analog output signals (0-10V or 0/4-20mA) compatible with [product_name].

Hello [user_name], thank you for your reply. I am primarily a software developer and new to PLCs. In addition to [product_name], I saw another option here: [url]. Could you recommend the additional hardware required for energy measurement? Also, could you help clarify the differences between [product_name] and [company_name] PLCs? We’re building an industrial product prototype, which may move to mass production if successful. Regarding the integrated web server you mentioned, does it offer an API for remote control and energy tracking? I found a Python wrapper for PLCs ([url]), hence my original question about Python. As a newcomer to PLCs, any advice or parts list would be greatly appreciated. Thank you.
You can't really compare [product_name] to [version_no]. They are fundamentally different devices. [product_name] is a programmable relay, while [version_no] is a full-featured PLC.

I think [product_name] could be workable for our needs. Is it the best fit for what I described? Does [product_name] offer an API interface for server-based control, or would I need a Python wrapper? If [product_name] is suitable, can you advise on hardware for energy measurement with it? Thanks.
For effective energy management, a [version_no] device would likely be a better choice than [product_name].

Because mass production may follow the pilot, using [version_no] could increase our equipment costs. Also, programming a [company_name] PLC seems more complex. Is there any practical way to measure energy consumption with [product_name]? What potential issues should I expect if I choose [product_name]? Thank you.
To assist, we need more details about your project. Please specify the hardware, and the required number of digital and analog inputs and outputs.

Let me provide more detail while avoiding any private information. The system will operate with an input power of 20KW to 30KW 3-phase AC and will activate only one of 3 or 5 outputs at a time—meaning input power is routed to one selected output. We also need a power consumption measurement unit at the input. The active output should be controllable by programming, through an API or wrapper. Does this specification help you provide guidance? Thank you.
Sorry, I’m unable to assist further. Perhaps another user may be able to help.
Thank you for your help so far. Do you think this project might be too complex? Can you refer someone else who could assist, or advise if I should post in another topic?

Posting another question isn’t an issue, but it looks like you’re seeking complete project management help. That's not the purpose here, as contributors help in their spare time. If you have specific questions about [product_name], someone will likely assist, but if you lack foundational knowledge, you may need to add an expert to your team. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion centers on whether [product_name] or [company_name] controllers (such as [version_no]) can meet the needs for remote pump control and reliable energy measurement in an industrial setting. Users compare options based on technical ability, programming simplicity, budget concerns, and the availability of remote management interfaces like web APIs or Python wrappers. There are doubts about [product_name]'s adequacy for advanced energy management versus more robust but costlier [company_name] controllers.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants a cost-effective, scalable industrial solution offering programmable remote control (preferably via Python or API) and accurate energy measurement for pumps. Integration should allow reliable, industrial-grade performance without unnecessary complexity or high costs.
